```{r setup}
#| include: false
RANDOM_SEED <- 42
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)

library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(randomForest)
library(gbm)
library(glmnet)
library(doParallel)
library(foreach)
library(tidyverse)
library(DT)
```

## Modeling objective

PBS Utah needs a short, reviewable list of lower-level donors for Major Gifts
staff to contact. This document compares models by their ability to rank
eligible constituents, rather than by classification accuracy alone.

The target is whether an eligible constituent will give **$2,000 to $15,000 in
the following fiscal year**. Eligibility at the decision date is annual giving
greater than $0 and less than $2,000. This keeps the modeling population aligned
with the stated lower-level-donor prospecting use case.

The training period is FY2021--FY2024. FY2025 is held out as a chronological
test: all FY2025 predictors were known at the decision date and its outcome is
FY2026 giving. The final scorecard emphasizes precision and lift in the first
100 and 250 constituents, which are more meaningful to a finite outreach team
than overall accuracy.

```{r read-data}
analytic <- read.csv(
  "Data_Files/constituent_fiscal_year_analytic.csv"
)

quality_report <- read.csv(
  "Data_Files/feature_engineering_quality_report.csv"
)

datatable(quality_report, caption = "Feature-engineering quality checks")
```

## Data review and feature exclusions

The engineering report documents that duplicate/copy artifacts were removed
through link, amount, date, and duplicate checks—not by using synthetic ID
labels. The report should be retained with the analysis for auditability.

The following columns are deliberately excluded from modeling:

- `constituent_id`: join and review key, never a predictor.
- `next_fy_*`: future outcomes; using them would leak the answer.
- `*_snapshot`: end-of-data constituent snapshots. They are useful dashboard
  context but are not known historically for every fiscal-year scoring record.
- `cultivation_*`: selection/contact/holdout are program-assignment fields,
  not pre-contact donor characteristics. They belong in a separate cultivation
  effect analysis, not in a prospect score.
- `fiscal_year`: used to create the chronological split, not a donor feature.

```{r build-model-frame}
TARGET_MIN <- 2000
TARGET_MAX <- 15000
TRAIN_YEARS <- 2021:2024
TEST_YEAR <- 2025
CONTACT_LIST_SIZES <- c(100, 250)

model_frame <- analytic %>%
  filter(
    fiscal_year %in% c(TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEAR),
    annual_giving > 0,
    annual_giving < TARGET_MIN,
    !is.na(next_fy_giving)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    target_range_next_fy = factor(
      if_else(next_fy_giving >= TARGET_MIN & next_fy_giving <= TARGET_MAX,
              "yes", "no"),
      levels = c("yes", "no")
    )
  )

outcome_columns <- c(
  "next_fy_giving", "next_fy_reached_2000", "next_fy_giving_growth",
  "target_range_next_fy"
)

excluded_columns <- names(model_frame)[
  names(model_frame) == "constituent_id" |
    names(model_frame) == "fiscal_year" |
    names(model_frame) %in% outcome_columns |
    str_detect(names(model_frame), "_snapshot$") |
    str_detect(names(model_frame), "^cultivation_")
]

# All remaining engineered predictors are numeric. Keeping the type restriction
# prevents accidental use of an unreviewed text or identifier field.
predictor_columns <- model_frame %>%
  select(-all_of(excluded_columns)) %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

feature_audit <- model_frame %>%
  summarise(across(
    all_of(predictor_columns),
    list(
      missing_rate = ~ mean(is.na(.x)),
      distinct_values = ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      zero_rate = ~ mean(.x == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("feature", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(missing_rate|distinct_values|zero_rate)$") %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_rate), distinct_values)

datatable(feature_audit, caption = "Candidate-predictor audit")

zero_variance_features <- names(nearZeroVar(model_frame[predictor_columns], saveMetrics = TRUE) %>%
  rownames_to_column("feature") %>%
  filter(nzv) %>%
  pull(feature))

if (length(zero_variance_features) > 0) {
  cat("Near-zero-variance features removed before modeling:\n")
  print(zero_variance_features)
  predictor_columns <- setdiff(predictor_columns, zero_variance_features)
} else {
  cat("No near-zero-variance features were found.\n")
}

model_data <- model_frame %>%
  select(constituent_id, fiscal_year, target_range_next_fy, all_of(predictor_columns))

train_data <- model_data %>% filter(fiscal_year %in% TRAIN_YEARS)
test_data <- model_data %>% filter(fiscal_year == TEST_YEAR)

stopifnot(nrow(train_data) > 0, nrow(test_data) > 0)
stopifnot(n_distinct(train_data$target_range_next_fy) == 2)
stopifnot(n_distinct(test_data$target_range_next_fy) == 2)

# caret's formula interface calls `na.fail()` before its `preProcess` argument
# can impute values. Create missingness indicators, then impute predictors with
# training-period medians only. This avoids both model errors and test-set
# leakage. A zero fallback is used only when a training feature is entirely NA.
missing_predictors <- predictor_columns[
  vapply(train_data[predictor_columns], function(x) any(is.na(x)), logical(1))
]

for (column in missing_predictors) {
  indicator <- paste0(column, "_missing")
  train_data[[indicator]] <- as.integer(is.na(train_data[[column]]))
  test_data[[indicator]] <- as.integer(is.na(test_data[[column]]))

  training_median <- median(train_data[[column]], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(training_median)) training_median <- 0

  train_data[[column]][is.na(train_data[[column]])] <- training_median
  test_data[[column]][is.na(test_data[[column]])] <- training_median
}

predictor_columns <- c(predictor_columns, paste0(missing_predictors, "_missing"))

stopifnot(!anyNA(train_data[predictor_columns]))
stopifnot(!anyNA(test_data[predictor_columns]))

bind_rows(
  train_data %>% summarise(split = "Training FY2021--FY2024", records = n(), positive_rate = mean(target_range_next_fy == "yes")),
  test_data %>% summarise(split = "Chronological test FY2025", records = n(), positive_rate = mean(target_range_next_fy == "yes"))
) %>% datatable(caption = "Eligible prospect population")
```

## Base model training

### Parallel processing setup

```{r parallel-setup}
n_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
registerDoParallel(cl)
cat("Using", foreach::getDoParWorkers(), "cores\n")
```

### Cross-validation setup

The held-out fiscal year is never used to choose a model. Repeated
cross-validation within the training years tunes models using ROC AUC; the
separate chronological test determines which model creates the strongest
contact list.

```{r cv-setup}
cv_control <- trainControl(
  method = "repeatedcv",
  number = 5,
  repeats = 2,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  allowParallel = TRUE
)

model_formula <- as.formula("target_range_next_fy ~ .")
train_model_data <- train_data %>% select(-constituent_id, -fiscal_year)
test_model_data <- test_data %>% select(-constituent_id, -fiscal_year)
```

### Logistic regression

```{r logistic}
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
log_model <- train(
  model_formula, data = train_model_data, method = "glm", family = "binomial",
  metric = "ROC", preProcess = c("medianImpute", "nzv"), trControl = cv_control
)
```

### Decision tree

```{r decision-tree}
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
tree_model <- train(
  model_formula, data = train_model_data, method = "rpart", metric = "ROC",
  preProcess = c("medianImpute", "nzv"), trControl = cv_control, tuneLength = 8
)
```

### Random forest

```{r random-forest}
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
rf_model <- train(
  model_formula, data = train_model_data, method = "rf", metric = "ROC",
  ntree = 500, importance = TRUE, preProcess = c("medianImpute", "nzv"),
  trControl = cv_control, tuneLength = 4
)
```

### Gradient boosting

```{r gradient-boosting}
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
gbm_model <- train(
  model_formula, data = train_model_data, method = "gbm", metric = "ROC",
  verbose = FALSE, preProcess = c("medianImpute", "nzv"),
  trControl = cv_control, tuneLength = 5
)
```

### Regularized logistic regression

```{r regularized-logistic}
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
enet_model <- train(
  model_formula, data = train_model_data, method = "glmnet", family = "binomial",
  metric = "ROC", preProcess = c("medianImpute", "nzv", "center", "scale"),
  trControl = cv_control,
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(
    alpha = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
    lambda = 10^seq(-4, 0, length.out = 8)
  )
)
```

### Bagged decision trees

```{r bagging}
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
bag_model <- train(
  model_formula, data = train_model_data, method = "treebag", metric = "ROC",
  preProcess = c("medianImpute", "nzv"), trControl = cv_control
)
```

## Model comparison: ranked contact lists

### Cross-validation results

```{r cv-results}
get_cv_metrics <- function(model, model_name) {
  best <- model$bestTune
  results <- model$results
  for (parameter in names(best)) {
    results <- results[results[[parameter]] == best[[parameter]], , drop = FALSE]
  }
  tibble(
    model = model_name,
    cv_auc = round(results$ROC[1], 4),
    cv_sensitivity = round(results$Sens[1], 4),
    cv_specificity = round(results$Spec[1], 4)
  )
}

models <- list(
  "Logistic regression" = log_model,
  "Decision tree" = tree_model,
  "Random forest" = rf_model,
  "Gradient boosting" = gbm_model,
  "Elastic net" = enet_model,
  "Bagged trees" = bag_model
)

cv_comparison <- imap_dfr(models, get_cv_metrics) %>% arrange(desc(cv_auc))
datatable(cv_comparison, caption = "Cross-validation comparison")
```

### Chronological test-list metrics

The primary evaluation is the quality of the ranked outreach list. Precision at
K answers: “Of the first K constituents staff review, what share actually
reached the target range next year?” Lift compares that result with contacting
K eligible constituents at random.

```{r contact-list-functions}
contact_list_metrics <- function(model, model_name, test_frame, list_sizes) {
  scored <- test_frame %>%
    mutate(probability = predict(model, newdata = test_model_data, type = "prob")$yes) %>%
    arrange(desc(probability))

  baseline_rate <- mean(scored$target_range_next_fy == "yes")

  map_dfr(list_sizes, function(k) {
    reviewed <- slice_head(scored, n = min(k, nrow(scored)))
    precision <- mean(reviewed$target_range_next_fy == "yes")
    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      contact_list_size = nrow(reviewed),
      precision_at_k = precision,
      lift_at_k = precision / baseline_rate,
      prospects_reaching_target = sum(reviewed$target_range_next_fy == "yes"),
      captured_share_of_all_targets = sum(reviewed$target_range_next_fy == "yes") /
        sum(scored$target_range_next_fy == "yes")
    )
  })
}

contact_list_results <- imap_dfr(
  models,
  ~ contact_list_metrics(.x, .y, test_data, CONTACT_LIST_SIZES)
) %>%
  arrange(contact_list_size, desc(precision_at_k), desc(lift_at_k))

datatable(contact_list_results, caption = "Chronological test: ranked contact-list performance")
```

### Test-set diagnostic metrics

These secondary diagnostics help identify models with strong ranking but poor
probability behavior. They should not outweigh the contact-list metrics in the
selection decision.

```{r test-diagnostics}
test_diagnostics <- imap_dfr(models, function(model, model_name) {
  probabilities <- predict(model, newdata = test_model_data, type = "prob")$yes
  roc_object <- roc(test_data$target_range_next_fy, probabilities, levels = c("no", "yes"), quiet = TRUE)
  tibble(
    model = model_name,
    test_auc = as.numeric(auc(roc_object)),
    test_pr_auc = prSummary(
      data.frame(obs = test_data$target_range_next_fy, yes = probabilities, no = 1 - probabilities),
      lev = c("yes", "no")
    )["AUC"]
  )
}) %>% arrange(desc(test_auc))

datatable(test_diagnostics, caption = "Chronological-test diagnostic metrics")
```

### Review checklist before selecting a final model

- Prefer the model with the strongest, stable precision/lift at the actual
  contact-list size PBS Utah can staff.
- Compare its results at both 100 and 250 names; avoid selecting a model on a
  trivial improvement at only one cutoff.
- Review the highest-ranked constituents with fundraising staff for face
  validity and inappropriate records.
- Check whether the list is dominated by current sustainers or another segment
  that would not represent a useful Major Gifts pipeline.
- Consider interpretability, maintainability, and score stability alongside the
  test metrics.

### End processing setup

```{r stop-parallel}
stopCluster(cl)
registerDoSEQ()
cat("Parallel processing stopped\n")
```
